title: Wren and Custard's Soft Nest
markdown:
The garden was bright, and a little job was peeking out from behind the red poppies.

In a garden kissed by sunshine lived a robin named Wren. She had a chest as red as a juicy berry and a chirp like tiny happy bells. Wren was busy making a super-cosy nest for her sleepy chicks, high in the big oak tree.

One sunny morning Wren chirped to her friend Custard, who was fluffy like warm milk.

“Custard, my friend,” she whispered. “I need the very softest fluff for our nest. We must be very quiet, for the chicks are sleeping soundly.”

Custard the cat stretched with a big slow yawn. His purr rumbled, gentle like far-away waves. “I will help you, Wren. We will be as quiet as moonbeams on water.”

That was the thing. Soft fluff was everywhere. Quiet was harder. Custard’s nose liked to twitch. Wren’s wings liked to hurry.

Wren hopped ahead, and Custard padded softly behind. They tiptoed to the edge of the sunny meadow.

Wren spotted fluffy white dandelions dancing. “Perfect fluff,” she whispered.

Custard blinked his green eyes. “Remember. Extra quiet for the sleeping chicks.”

Wren pecked a dandelion puff. Soft seeds danced like tiny fairies. Some tickled Custard’s nose and made his whiskers wiggle with a silent giggle.

Then Custard spotted something soft and white on a clothesline, like a fluffy cloud.

“Wren,” he meowed, his voice a gentle rumble. “That looks as soft as a hundred dandelions.”

Wren landed on the clothesline. Oh, it was soft. They each took a bit. Wren nudged it with her beak, and Custard patted it with his paw. They moved like a quiet dance.

“Patience now,” whispered Wren, as another puff tickled Custard’s nose.

He could not help it. He let out a tiny quiet sneeze, like a soft sigh. The sleepy chicks did not stir one bit. They just dreamed sweet happy dreams.

Wren waited with her head tilted, listening. Then she took the next puff more slowly. Custard held his whiskers still on purpose.

They gathered more and more fluff. Wren’s quick pecks and Custard’s gentle pats worked together like a happy song. Wren’s little chest puffed out, and a soft happy trill escaped her. Custard’s purr hummed a happy tune.

Their fluff was ready. They carried it back to the nest, a quiet ballet of soft movements and happy purrs. Wren’s nest was a wonderful sight. The fluff made it so soft and inviting, like a warm hug.

Wren looked at Custard, her bright eyes sparkling. “Thank you, Custard,” she chirped. “You were the kindest friend.”

Custard dipped his head, his tail giving a gentle swish. “And you, Wren, are the best nest-maker.”

As the sun began to set, painting the sky with soft colours, the baby chicks snuggled deeper into their super-soft nest. They slept on, undisturbed. Wren and Custard sat side by side, their hearts full of quiet joy.

The poppies nodded. The clothesline, now a little less fluffy, swayed. And the nest, which had needed the softest stuff in the garden, held every small sleeping breath.
